incident-bot: ALERT: Runtime-prod cluster - repeated OOMs on gpu-pool-2, autoscaler flapping. Severity P1, check logs and notify oncall :rotating_light:
jen_oncall: I'm on call. pulling p99/p95 for the last 30m, assigning tasks. can someone grab `nvidia-smi` snapshots and node memory histograms for gpu-prod-{01,02,03}?
devon: grabbing now. running: `for n in gpu-prod-01 gpu-prod-02 gpu-prod-03; do ssh $n 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv' ; done` output pasted below 
```
Time, index, memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
15:02:10, 0, 1200, 16384
15:02:10, 1, 1188, 16384
15:03:05, 0, 15600, 16384
15:03:05, 1, 15630, 16384
15:04:20, 0, 16240, 16384
```
ryan: oof looks like memory approaching full on multiple cards, fragmentation/eviction happening. any recent config changes or heavy batches?
maya: saw a surge of large batch generate calls from acct `acme-inc` route `/v1/generate` around 15:02. their batch_size jumped to 64 in a couple of requests. we have KV-cache warmups spiking too.
andre: hypothesis: KV-cache + oversized batches pushed working set beyond available VRAM -> allocator fragmentation -> OOM. also some pinned tensors from model variant `titan-q8` not releasing quickly.
jen_oncall: mitigation idea: 1) throttle acme-inc (rate limit their key) 2) temporarily reduce `max_batch_size` for titan-q8 from 64 -> 16 3) disable prefix caching for that model while we stabilize. who can patch the routing policy?
devon: applying patch to routing cfg now. `kubectl -n inference patch cm routing-config --type merge -p '{"acme-inc": {"rate_limit": 5}}'`
ops_bot: deploy-bot: configmap routing-config updated (rev 892) by devon.
ryan: lowering batch size on runtime pool with hotfix: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/hotfix -d '{"model":"titan-q8","max_batch":16}'` -- applied. confirm responses starting to fall.
maya: also disabled KV prefix cache for that model: `PATCH /models/titan-q8/cache { "prefix_cache": false }` done.
jen_oncall: monitor for 5m and report errors and 5xx rate. also collect `dmesg` and allocator logs from the three nodes while we watch. please paste dmesg snippets if you see page faults/oom-killer.
devon: dmesg from gpu-prod-02 shows repeated page allocations and gpu driver warnings, pasted: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus` then `oom-killer invoked for process runtime-server`
ryan: customer impact: between 15:02-15:10 we saw ~0.6% elevated 5xx and ~150 failed requests from acme-inc. downstream apps reported latency spikes. notifying support to open ticket.
jen_oncall: good. looks like mitigations reduced OOMs. memory used now: 15:12 snapshots show ~8-10GB used per card, previously 16GB.
maya: saving logs + `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` and kernel alloc logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/3344556677/.
andre: next steps for RCA: 1) timeline reconstruction (request traces + kvcache metrics) 2) heap/allocator sampling (gcore/pprof) 3) replay workload if possible and test batch-size threshold 4) recommend permanent guardrails (per-customer batch caps, cache eviction heuristics).
jen_oncall: handing off to ryan for follow-up. ryan you're on for the next 8 hours, collect evidence and prepare RCA doc. I'll remain reachable for coordination.
ryan: ack. onboarding notes: run `collect-alloc-trace --nodes gpu-prod-* --since 15:00 --out s3://redwood-incident-logs/3344556677/alloc-traces` and include `kv_cache_stats` + `batch_histogram` from ingest logs. will post initial RCA draft in #incidents tomorrow.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, OOM rate returned to baseline. severity downgraded to P2. follow-up RCA assigned to ryan.
jen_oncall: tagging @support to contact Acme and offer remediation + incident summary. thanks team :thumbsup:
